extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and measurement standards for compiling and interpreting WIPO IP statistics (patents, utility models, trademarks, industrial designs, geographical indications) for calendar-year comparison and cross-jurisdictional analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary use of application data as measure of IP activity
rubrics_metrics.description: IP Facts and Figures ... focuses primarily on application data, the most often used measure of IP activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use applications as the primary indicator when comparing IP activity across jurisdictions and time. When using application counts, note the specific counting conventions for different IP rights (see trademark class count and design count entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark application class count
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark application data refer to class counts – that is, the number of classes specified in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To compare trademark filing activity across offices with differing filing systems, use class counts rather than simple application counts. The class count captures the number of Nice classes specified; apply caution when comparing single-class versus multi-class filing systems (some offices require separate applications per class).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design application design count
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial design data refer to design counts, that is, the number of designs contained in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use design counts to compare filing activity across offices that allow multiple designs per application versus those that allow only one. Under the Hague System, up to 100 designs may be protected in a single application, so counting designs (not applications) yields more comparable measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Application' and 'Application abroad'
rubrics_metrics.description: Application: The procedure for requesting IP rights at an office ... Also refers to a set of documents submitted to an office by the applicant. Application abroad: For statistical purposes, an application filed by a resident of a given state or jurisdiction with the IP office of another state or jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compiling by-origin statistics, classify an application filed by a resident in another jurisdiction as an 'application abroad' from the perspective of the applicant's origin. Distinguish this from non-resident applications seen by receiving offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Resident' and 'Resident application'
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident: For statistical purposes, a resident application refers to an application filed with the IP office of, or acting for, the state or jurisdiction in which the first named applicant in the application is resident. Resident applications are sometimes referred to as 'domestic applications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting resident filings by origin, use the residence of the first named applicant (or assignee in jurisdictions where that is the convention) to determine origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of application (country or region) convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin (country or region) For statistical purposes, the origin of an application means the country or territory of residence of the first named applicant in the application. In some cases (notably in the United States of America), the country of origin is determined by the residence of the assignee rather than that of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document any deviations from the 'first named applicant' rule (e.g., where assignee residence is used) when merging datasets from different offices to avoid misattributing origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal coverage and growth definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise stated, all data refer to activity that occurred in calendar year 2023. Growth means annual growth, that is, the change from 2022 to 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use calendar-year 2023 as the baseline unless a specific indicator states otherwise; compute growth as year-on-year change (2023 vs 2022). Note possible later updates to the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source and update caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024. Please note that owing to the continual updating of statistics, data presented in this publication may differ from data previously published, and also from the data available on WIPO’s web pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always cite the WIPO Statistics Database and the extraction date; be prepared for revisions and document the data extract timestamp in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting of Madrid and Hague system designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Application class count is the sum of classes specified in applications filed by applicants plus, where applicable, those specified in designations made via the Madrid System. Application design count is the sum of designs contained in applications filed by applicants plus, where applicable, those contained in designations made via the Hague System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Madrid/Hague designations in class/design counts when producing origin-level aggregates that incorporate international filings via these WIPO systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of GDP-normalized rates (per USD 100 billion PPP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident patent applications per USD 100 billion GDP ... Note: GDP data are in 2021 US purchasing power parity (PPP) dollars. The top 10 origins were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 25 billion PPP and more than 100 resident patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing filing intensity across economies, normalize counts by GDP (reported here per USD 100 billion PPP) and apply selection thresholds (e.g., minimum GDP and minimum application counts) to avoid distortions from very small economies or tiny sample sizes. Document the GDP year and PPP basis used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for origin-based comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: The top 10 origins were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 25 billion PPP and more than 100 resident patent applications. (Other selection thresholds described elsewhere, e.g., trademarks: GDP > USD 575 billion PPP and resident trademark class count of at least 46,000.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply specified inclusion thresholds when reproducing ranked tables/figures to ensure comparability with the WIPO publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-sector grouping (trademarks and designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the Nice Classification, trademark applications can be categorized into 10 industry sectors. Grouping the 32 Locarno classes into 12 industry sectors serves to highlight the most important industry sectors for designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map Nice classes to the 10 industry sectors for trademarks and Locarno classes to 12 sectors for designs when producing sectoral breakdowns. State the mapping used, as sector aggregation choices affect rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'In force'
rubrics_metrics.description: In force Refers to IP rights that are currently valid or, in the case of trademarks, active. To remain in force, IP protection must be maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When counting 'rights in force', include only active/valid rights per the maintaining office's status; account for renewal/maintenance requirements that affect whether a right remains in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent definition and typical term
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent A set of exclusive rights granted by law to applicants for inventions that are new, non-obvious and commercially applicable. A patent is valid for a limited period (generally 20 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting patent statistics, understand that patents are granted for inventions meeting novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability; term lengths and examination practices vary by jurisdiction and affect counts of rights in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model definition and measurement note
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model (UM) is a special form of patent right. It has less stringent requirements than a patent but gives a shorter term of protection. Utility models are not available in every jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat utility model filings separately from patent filings and note jurisdictional availability. Include UMs in aggregate analyses where appropriate but avoid conflating them with full patents given differing legal requirements and terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-counting caveat for geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Data received by WIPO from a total of 86 national and regional authorities show there were an estimated 58,600 protected geographical indications (GIs) in existence in 2023. It is important to note that this overall total will inevitably include a degree of double counting, as GIs in force through bilateral, plurilateral or multilateral agreements could potentially be included multiple times. If GIs in force through various international agreements are excluded, then around 23,400 GIs were in force in 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aggregating GIs across authorities, account for double counting caused by regional systems (e.g., EU) and international registrations (Lisbon System); report both gross totals and de-duplicated estimates where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on origin data over office data (edition-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike past editions, this year's publication places more emphasis on origin data as opposed to office data when presenting many of its indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reproducing or comparing with past editions, note the shift in emphasis (origin vs office) and adjust interpretation accordingly. Be explicit whether figures are presented by origin (applicant residence) or by receiving office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for missing or zero data
rubrics_metrics.description: .. indicates either zero, not available, or not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading or reproducing tables, treat '..' as indicating missing/unavailable/not applicable and document how such cases are handled in any analysis (e.g., imputation, exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation guidance for drivers of change (resident vs abroad filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For example: 'For China-based applicants, an increase in resident filings was the main driver of overall growth, whereas for those based in Switzerland, an increase in abroad filings was the main contributor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing growth, decompose changes into resident and abroad (international) filings to identify domestic versus international drivers. Present both components to explain aggregate trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of WIPO Statistical tools and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The WIPO IP Statistics Data Center is a free online service for accessing WIPO statistics on patents, utility models, trademarks, industrial designs and the use of the PCT, Madrid and Hague Systems. Users can select from a wide range of indicators to view or download data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the IP Statistics Data Center and IP Statistical Country Profiles as canonical data sources; these tools are available in multiple languages and intended for IP professionals, researchers and policymakers.
